channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Witkoff: Putin’s Messenger?
item.description: What did Steve Witkoff know about Russia when he was first sent to see President Putin in February last year?
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: The closely-watched Lindsay Clancy trial ends with one last dramatic moment
item.description: The closely watched case of the Massachusetts mother who killed her three young children was on the verge of being declared a mistrial Friday — but there was still one more dramatic moment to come.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Wallace & Gromit' creators turn 50 with spook-tacular Shaun yarn
item.description: Crochet hook in hand, the animator slightly raises the eyelid of a clay model sheep in a filmmaking technique as old as cinema, perfected over five decades by Aardman Animations.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: UN approves resolution in support of map that shows Africa's true size
item.description: The United Nations on ‌Friday voted for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting countries' true size, a resolution sponsored by African states to counter perceptions that the continent is peripheral.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Rain man’ to the rescue? France’s ex-president Hollande plots unlikely comeback
item.description: Once so deeply unpopular he had to give up running for a second term in office, former French president François Hollande has slipped back into the conversation ahead of next year’s Élysée Palace race, hoping voters put off by squabbling candidates will come to see him as a safe – if unexciting – pair of hands after a decade of Emmanuel Macron’s ‘disruptive’ presidency.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin DODMAN

item.title: Chinese national rescued from Nepal tunnel 10 days after flash flood
item.description: A Chinese national was pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal on Saturday, authorities said, 10 ‌days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through a Himalayan valley, killing more than 1,300 people.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: War in Ukraine: Putin, Zelensky order pause in strikes
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Moscow for talks on peace in Ukraine
item.description: US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow on Saturday for talks on how to end the ‌war in Ukraine, where they were met by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Our guest Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Culture of fear within US Defence Department: Slow leakage of dissent against the administration'
item.description: Catherine Viette is pleased to welcome Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth. He argues that the turmoil surrounding Pete Hegseth points to a problem much deeper than personnel disputes at the Pentagon: The removal and marginalization of experienced officials, the weakening of professional military education, and the prioritization of political loyalty risk changing the institutional culture through which the US military evaluates strategy and challenges political authority.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Paris hosts African Diaspora International Film Festival
item.description:
This weekend, Paris is hosting the 16th edition of FIFDA, the African Diaspora International Film Festival.
From September 4 to 6, 15 films from 13 countries will be screened, spanning fiction and non-fiction, as well as feature-length and short films. The festival provides a space to explore how contemporary societies face and overcome wounds from the past, while giving a voice to members of African diasporas.
Guest Lawrence Cole, co-executive producer of "Shadow of Greed", and Diarah N'Daw-Spech, FIFDA co-founder and co-director.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Uber announces immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda
item.description: Uber has announced its immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda. The decision comes amid a global restructuring, but mainly as Uber has lost significant ground to its competitors in both countries.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: UN experts urge Sudan-wide arms embargo
item.description: A weapons embargo must be extended to the whole of Sudan, and it must be enforced. That is, in essence, the conclusion of a UN experts' report presented to the Human Rights Council. The report also points to the responsibility of foreign entities in a conflict that has now been raging for more than three years. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal: Two more people rescued alive
item.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Witkoff and Kushner are in Moscow in a new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian state news outlets reported. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Emmanuel Macron unveils new disability strategy
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron delivered the closing speech at the national conference on disability. It is an event the government holds every three years. It aims to set or guide policies. Macron made disability one of the priorities of his first five-year term. Since 2017, the government has implemented a number of measures to better integrate people with disabilities into society. According to official figures, between 5.7 and 18.2 million people aged five and older in France have a disability. We discuss this with our guest, Dr. Johny Daniel, associate professor at the School of Education at Durham University.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Presidential campaigning kicks off in France ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: On April 18th and May 2nd next year - France will be voting to elect a new president to replace Emmanuel Macron. The country's latest opinion polls predict a victory for Marine le Pen of the Far-right National Rally. Although the election is still over seven months away, many potential candidates have already thrown their hats into the ring. But do any of them stand a chance of beating the far right? Our guest Eleanor Beardsley from National Public Radio answers that question.
item.dc:creator: Catherine VIETTE

item.title: Two Nepal rescues revive hopes 10 days after flood
item.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled alive on Saturday a Chinese national from a tunnel and a local woman from her partially submerged home, as emergency response teams searched with renewed vigour for thousands missing since catastrophic flooding 10 days ago. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: DR Congo: Ebola burial teams race against time
item.description:
In eastern DR Congo, Ebola burial teams are racing against time as the outbreak continues to spread.
They face a dangerous mission: safely burying victims while dealing with distrust and threats from local communities.
The response is further complicated by the ongoing rebel conflict in the region.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US ambassador to Israel visits Palestinian town hit by West Bank settler violence
item.description: US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Saturday visited Turmus Ayya, a Palestinian town in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that has been repeatedly targeted by Israeli settler violence. Huckabee, a staunch supporter of Israel and its illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory, said that it was in the Israeli government's interests to take action against violent settlers.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Bangladesh measles toll nears grim 1,000-child mark
item.description: Bangladesh's deadliest measles outbreak in decades is nearing the grim milestone of 1,000 child deaths, as a devastating epidemic sweeps through the country and crowded hospital wards fill with struggling babies.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'I don't know if I'm dreaming': Rebuilding lives after Nepal's devastating floods
item.description: With thousands of people driven from their homes by a massive flash flood that swept entire villages away, FRANCE 24 visits a school in Nepal's remote Rasuwa district that has been converted to a temporary shelter for the dispossessed.
item.dc:creator: Shahzaib WAHLAH

item.title: Germany: AfD eyes historic state election win
item.description:
In Saxony-Anhalt, AfD – Germany's far-right party – is polling at 40% or more of voting intentions, just days ahead of the regional election on 6 September 2026. If the AfD wins an absolute majority of seats, it could soon be in charge here. It would be the first time since 1945 that a far-right party has led a German region.
To get there, the party is banking on the promise of a return to "the Germany of old", leaning on East German symbols such as Simson mopeds and retro aesthetics. It is a well-established strategy that draws on a gnawing sense of decline for decades and increasing distrust of traditional parties.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal: Temporary education centres help flood-displaced children
item.description:
Children displaced by flash floods in Nepal are attending a temporary education centre in Nuwakot, while aid organisations work to support devastated communities.
The UN estimates that $158 million worth of buildings have been damaged, with Nepal warning that reconstruction could cost billions.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
